residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a resident of Iowa for at least one year prior to filing, unless the defendant is a resident of Iowa at the time of filing.

waitingPeriod.description: No decree shall be entered until 90 days after the date the petition is served on the respondent. Iowa Code §598.19.

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown
noFault.description: There has been a breakdown of the marriage relationship to the extent that the legitimate objects of matrimony have been destroyed and there remains no reasonable likelihood that the marriage can be preserved

groundsForDissolution.notes: Iowa is a purely no-fault state. The only ground for dissolution is irretrievable breakdown of the marriage. Iowa Code §598.17.

propertyDivision.description: Iowa uses equitable distribution. ALL property of both spouses — including property acquired before the marriage — is subject to division. The court considers the length of the marriage, property brought into the marriage, each party's contribution, age and health, earning capacity, and other relevant factors.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Iowa does not recognize a separate property classification. All property of both spouses is in the marital pot, though the court considers when and how property was acquired.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirements — 1 year unless defendant is Iowa resident
Grounds for dissolution — irretrievable breakdown (no-fault only)
Property division — equitable distribution of all property
Child custody — joint legal custody, physical care, visitation
Iowa Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: Iowa filing fees are approximately $265 for a dissolution of marriage but may vary by county. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via an Application to Defer Fees.

basic.name: Original Notice
basic.description: Formal notice to respondent (Iowa equivalent of summons)

basic.name: Financial Affidavit
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Original Notice
service.description: Service on respondent via sheriff, process server, or certified mail

service.name: Voluntary Appearance and Waiver
service.description: Respondent waives formal service by voluntary appearance
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Child Support Computation Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Iowa Child Support Guidelines (Iowa Code §598.21B)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Iowa Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Iowa must file a response within 20 days of service (additional time may be granted)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Iowa uses an income shares model. Both parents' net monthly incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Iowa Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined net income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust. Adjustments may apply for overnight visitation credits.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Iowa provides three types of spousal support: (1) Traditional — ongoing support based on need and ability to pay, (2) Rehabilitative — temporary support to allow a spouse to become self-supporting through education or training, and (3) Reimbursement — compensation for economic sacrifices made during the marriage (e.g., supporting a spouse through school).
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: The court considers the length of the marriage, age and health of the parties, earning capacity, education level, feasibility of becoming self-supporting, and tax consequences.

court.name: District Court
court.description: Dissolution of marriage is filed in the District Court in the county where either party resides.
